title: Parse a requirements.txt file
description: Write a function `parse_requirements(text)` that parses `pip freeze`-style content and returns a list of `(name, version)` tuples - one per `name==version` line. Blank lines and `#`-comments (whether on their own line or trailing after a requirement) are ignored.
starter_code:

hints: 💡 Idea to consider: process the file one line at a time, stripping comments before checking anything else
text.splitlines() gives you one line per requirement; splitting each line on '#' and keeping only the part before it removes both whole-line and trailing comments in the same step.

For each non-blank line left after stripping comments, split on '==' to get the package name and version - a regular expression like ^([\w.-]+)==([\w.-]+)$ (or a plain .split('==', 1)) pulls both parts out.
expected_behavior: Returns (name, version) tuples for every requirement line, comments and blank lines skipped.
explanation: Stripping comments before anything else means the rest of the parsing never has to think about '#' at all - splitting on '==' or matching a regex only ever sees a clean 'name==version' string by that point.
